Targeting and posts are set up, and all 6 promoted posts show ACCEPTED. Activating now.
The campaign is live (RUNNING). I'll check back in about 6 hours.
Early numbers, mostly overnight hours: 5.5K impressions, 1 link click, $2.69 spent. All posts are approved. Too soon to judge anything. I'll check again around midday Central.

At the 42-hour mark, I've spent $137.57 for 48 clicks, with Nashville costing far more per click ($4.51) than the rest of the US ($2.32). I'll shift more budget toward the cheaper national audience while keeping Nashville active, staying within the $700 cap.

content.text: New budgets: Nashville $25/day with a $190 total, rest of US $72/day with a $510 total. The combined cap is still $700. Next check is tomorrow.
Nashville's spend and clicks haven't changed since yesterday, even though it's still getting impressions. Checking whether that ad group is still serving.

Spend's on track — the flat Nashville numbers from 6/9 were just reporting lag, not a stall. Nashville clicks cost ~$4.68 each vs. ~$2.61 for the rest of the US, so since every signature counts equally, I'm shifting more budget to the cheaper US ad group.

content.text: New totals are $145 for Nashville and $555 for the rest of the US, which still adds up to the $700 cap. Next check is tomorrow.

The campaign ran Monday, June 7 through Monday, June 14 (Central). It spent **$682.77 of your $700**, delivered **673,108 impressions** and drove **216 link clicks** to larkspurshade.org/sign. X can't see signatures without the pixel, so your own petition count is the real result.

## Recap

| | Spend | Impressions | Link clicks | Cost per click |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Total** | **$682.77** | **673,108** | **216** | **$3.16** |
| Nashville metro, 18+ | $132.33 | 101,759 | 28 | $4.73 |
| Rest of US, 18+ | $550.44 | 571,349 | 188 | $2.93 |

**By post (both ad groups combined):**
- "Nashville bus stops get brutal…" (2195032901022795095): $271.87, 238,270 impressions, 88 clicks, $3.09 per click
- "The whole ask: one shade tree…" (2195214094957680647): $250.37, 235,647 impressions, 79 clicks, $3.17 per click
- "Summer heat is here…" (2195395288890401955): $160.53, 199,191 impressions, 49 clicks, $3.28 per click

## Setup and changes
- **Structure:** one campaign with two ad groups, optimized for link clicks. One targeted the Nashville metro and the other the rest of the US. Both were limited to ages 18+ to match your petition rule. Political campaigning ads may only use certain targeting types, and location and age are both allowed. X approved all three of your posts in both ad groups, and I didn't write any new ones.
- **Budget changes:** Nashville clicks cost more than clicks elsewhere in the US, so I moved money away from it twice (June 8 and June 10). The Nashville ad group's total cap went from $250 to $145, and the rest of the US went from $450 to $555. The combined total cap stayed at $700 throughout.
- **Shutdown:** the ad groups had a scheduled end of midnight Central on June 15. I also paused the campaign afterward, so nothing else will spend.

## Takeaways
- **Comparing your numbers:** 216 clicks reached your sign-up page. Comparing that with the signatures you collected June 7–14, especially any from X traffic, will give you a rough sign-up rate.
- **Nashville vs. the rest of the US:** a Nashville click cost about 60% more, but those signers are Metro Council's own residents. If local names matter more to the council than the national total, put more of the budget into Nashville next time.
- **Pixel:** if you plan to do this again, installing X's pixel would let X optimize for actual sign-ups rather than clicks.
